system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime

- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge deal team. All Seller material treated as the other side's draft; reviewed against the Buyer Playbook. **Overall: the Seller package is materially off-market and off-playbook on every limitation point and leaves all four key completion risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title) unresolved. Recommend a full mark-up rather than acceptance of any item as-is.**

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback only, and no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft exists, so it cannot be conceded.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl. 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery.
- Recommendation: **REJECT all three elements; revert to playbook figures and tipping basket.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure would forfeit the first AUD 250k of every valid claim.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion, plus a catch-all that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl. 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only to the claim categories expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback (no Amelia Frost sign-off) and the default-to-all language is a backdoor override of the separate regimes.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **REJECT outright.** Title and capacity are the foundation of the bargain; capping them at 20% for 18 months is unacceptable and not a simplicity issue.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) – i.e. no fraud carve-out at all.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; insert express, non-waivable fraud carve-out.** This is a non-negotiable playbook item and no one on our side has authority to waive it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch. 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **REJECT general disclosure; require fair-and-specific standard with cross-referenced disclosures.** Whole-data-room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranty package given the volume of material.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **DELETE cl. 8.3.** A "discoverable" constructive-knowledge bar combined with general disclosure (N-006) would remove virtually all warranty protection.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of a written consent (cl. 3/6.3). DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence conditions (cl. 11.3) are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: effective consent AND evidence that cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a Condition Precedent; not consent-on-delivery; not mere reasonable endeavours.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; make effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a hard CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and a conditional consent delivered without proof of satisfaction leaves the key customer relationship at risk post-Completion.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7). DL para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion; post-completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; require payout letter and releases as Completion deliverables with repayment through the funds flow.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and uncleared security still in place, and no Amelia Frost approval exists for a deferred release.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly seller-funded; no silent exclusion.
- Recommendation: **REJECT; add specific line item (bonuses + superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs) deducted from or funded by Seller.** Without this the Company bears the liability post-Completion and the Buyer effectively pays it twice.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl. 11.1). DL para 4: DD-004 cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on cleared payment of every fee; AUD 180,000 shown open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment; non-payment not independently verified.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering ownership/title to all SOW3 Project Materials and any related loss, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure; treat AUD 180k as unverified.
- Recommendation: **COUNTER with broadened indemnity + require evidence of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment at Completion.** The real exposure is a gap in IP ownership, not just the fee; the SOW3 cure path should be kept but the indemnity must cover the title consequence.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6). DL para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no confirmed breach or loss stated.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, pre-Completion status updates, and a specific indemnity for loss arising; make no assumption of confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric claim.
- Recommendation: **DO NOT ACCEPT the "not material" characterisation; require preservation/investigation covenants, update obligations and a specific indemnity, without asserting a breach.** The facts are genuinely undetermined and the Buyer should neither price it nor let the Seller close it off.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (DD-008/DD-011); silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of timing, terminability and accrual status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **ASSESS, do not concede or deduct yet; request terms, timing and termination rights before Completion.** Whether these are ordinary course or a Seller-era accrued liability turns on facts the Seller has not supplied.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: limitations "apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; tax and IP folded into the general regime; title treated the same (cl. 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims as separate, expressly defined categories with their own caps and periods; no hidden general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **REJECT the default-to-general construct; draft a limitation schedule that expressly allocates each category.** Three separate clauses collectively collapse every protection into the 20%/18-month/basket regime.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% of shares "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012". DL para 10 concedes this is the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence – ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, certified board/shareholder authorities, share certificates – not the Seller-supplied internal register.
- Recommendation: **REJECT as sufficient; commission independent searches and make clean results plus title warranties (under the N-004 regime) a Completion requirement.** An internal register the Seller controls is not independent proof of unencumbered ownership.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: treat as OPEN; separate tax and IP categories to be negotiated; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution either way.
- Recommendation: **DO NOT ACCEPT as settled; record Tax and IP as open items for a separate round.** Nothing in the Seller's draft has been agreed and these categories must be addressed on their own terms, not swept into N-014's general regime.

---

**Priority for the mark-up / next call:**
1. Deal-blockers: Bluefen CP (N-008), Riverlark releases at Completion (N-009), bonus funds flow (N-010), independent title evidence (N-015).
2. Structural fixes: fraud carve-out (N-005), category separation (N-014), fundamental regime (N-004), delete general disclosure and buyer-knowledge bar (N-006/N-007).
3. Economics: cap 25% (N-001), thresholds and tipping basket (N-002), 24 months (N-003).
4. Diligence follow-ups: Ironquay payment evidence (N-011), DD-006 investigation (N-012), Sandbar terms (N-013), Tax/IP schedule (N-016).

**Authority note:** no Amelia Frost written approvals exist for any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release). None of those positions should be signalled as acceptable to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
